title: Unresolved historical identifiers must remain reserved until immutable provenance resolves them

observed: operations/ACTIVE_QUEUE.json requires M-004, M-005, and M-006 to remain unresolved until exhaustive repository coverage and immutable provenance are obtained.
The queue's safe next action explicitly forbids recreating historical identifiers while coverage is incomplete.
CM-1025 preserves the rule that descriptive claims must not be treated as executable or evidentiary enforcement.
inferred: Reusing M-004, M-005, or M-006 for newly created artifacts would collapse two distinct identities: the unresolved historical claim and the new artifact.
A newly created artifact carrying one of those identifiers could be mistaken for recovered provenance even when no immutable origin object had been located.
Identifier reservation is therefore a provenance-preservation control, not merely a naming convention.
proposed: Treat M-004, M-005, and M-006 as reserved unresolved identifiers across continuity records, queue updates, tests, generated fixtures, and migration scripts.
Permit references to those identifiers only when claim_status remains unresolved or when an immutable locator is supplied and independently verified.
Assign fresh identifiers to all newly created artifacts rather than backfilling unresolved historical IDs.
Add a future machine-checkable identifier-reservation test once the authoritative artifact index or namespace registry is located.
superseded: Treating an unresolved identifier as available for reuse because its originating artifact is not currently located.
Treating semantic similarity or matching prose as sufficient to backfill an unresolved historical identifier.
unresolved: The authoritative namespace registry or originating decision source for M-004, M-005, and M-006 remains unlocated.
Exhaustive branch and commit-history coverage has not yet been demonstrated.
No machine-checkable repository-wide reservation test exists yet.

source_provenance.supports: The unresolved provenance objective, acceptance criteria, and explicit prohibition on recreating historical identifiers under incomplete coverage.
The distinction between descriptive assertions and enforceable provenance controls.
The evidence-gated rule for changing operational roles; no registry change is justified by this slice.

verification.method: Compared the exact current ACTIVE_QUEUE, SPECIALIST_REGISTRY, and CM-1025 blobs and derived the minimal fail-closed identifier rule consistent with their explicit constraints.
limitations: This record does not establish the original meaning of M-004, M-005, or M-006.
This record does not claim exhaustive repository coverage.
The reservation rule is recorded as a durable continuity decision but is not yet enforced by a repository-wide validator.

falsification_routes: Produce an immutable pre-existing artifact or decision source that assigns one of the identifiers and satisfies namespace, owner, semantic-role, temporal-precedence, and locator agreement.
Demonstrate an authoritative namespace policy explicitly allowing unresolved historical identifiers to be reused without provenance ambiguity.
Show a repository-wide validator that already prevents unresolved identifier reuse, making the proposed enforcement work redundant.
